result.title: Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation
result.comment: 50 pages, 20 figures; accepted for poster presentation at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Real-world generative problems in biology, medical imaging, or robotics, rarely come with perfectly paired source and target distributions. While unbalanced Optimal Transport (uOT) provides a robust framework to bridge unpaired datasets via minimum-length paths in probability space, existing formulations based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geometry introduce a structural bias toward high density regions, often triggering mode collapse. We introduce Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT), a novel uOT formulation grounded in contact geometry that decouples density transport direction from mass growth to eliminate structural bias. This allows CuOT to adapt sampling steps to the local data structure, naturally reducing step sizes in high-density regions to prevent overshooting and ensuring stable convergence. The result is a stable, scalable path-length minimization solver that consistently outperforms WFR-based methods on biological dynamics reconstruction, unpaired image-to-image translation, and video generation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出基于接触几何的非平衡最优传输公式 CuOT，通过将密度输运方向与质量增长解耦来消除 WFR 几何的高密度偏置，并用于生物动态重建、非配对图像翻译与视频生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作聚焦生成模型的传输路径与采样步长，既不涉及 VLM 内部 latent 推理状态、视觉证据使用或停止决策；其中按局部数据密度自适应调整步长仅为与动态计算的松散类比，缺少可核查的具体借鉴线索。
